differences.what: massing: the draft's 13 m hipped box is now the photograph's house: two tall storeys over a high basement under a slated mansard with a crested deck, the library pavilion at the south end carried up into a steep gable with a finial, the porch and balcony before the hall, and the steep slated pyramid over the north-east corner; the pavilion's finial prints at y 115 px against the photograph's 290 (the gable steeper and about 2 m taller than the photograph's), the pyramid's at y 45 against 100
the front's width: the body is widened to the 1911 outline's 14.2 m, and the pavilion's south edge, the porch and the corner now print within about 30-60 px of the photograph together
heights: the balcony's floor and the cornice's foot print within about 20 px of the photograph's (y 893 and 640 px)

the corner: the photograph's oriel at the second storey on a column over the cut corner, under its own small stone gable; the record stands a square brick tower across the corner from grade, its windowless base where the photograph shows the column and the open corner
the corner's pyramid: the photograph's springs from the mansard behind the oriel, wider at its foot and flared; the record's springs from the tower's own cornice

the library pavilion's gable: the photograph's has slated, flared cheeks with a carved panel and kneeler blocks; the record's is a plain coped brick gable, and the pavilion stands 0.8 m out where the plan draws about 1.25

the porch: the photograph's balcony runs from the pavilion to the parlour on stone piers and a cluster of three columns, with a carved stone balustrade about 0.85 m high; the record's hood is the hall's width on one column a side, railed 0.55 m with balusters
the stoop: the photograph's curved flight from the walk and second flight from the south, with carved stone cheeks; the record's single straight flight

the stone bands: the photograph's pale stone sill and spring courses, the stone panels under the principal lights and the stone dressings round every opening against the dark brick; the record shows only the stone basement and the kit's surrounds
the openings' heads: the photograph's principal-storey lights under stone arches and the pavilion's paired lights; the record's are square-headed two-over-two sash
the cornice: the photograph's paired blocks over a dentil band; the record's plain moulded stone cornice
the front dormers: the photograph's small flat-topped dormer over the hall and the large stone dormer with a roundel in its gable; the record's two gabled dormers without the roundel

the 21st Street flank: the photograph's narrow lights, its projecting bay with a balustraded top and the basement lights under sloped stone hoods; the record's lights at the kit's spacing and its one-storey canted bay

the iron fence: the photograph's low scrolled panels on a stone curb between square stone piers with pyramidal caps, turning along 21st Street; the record's K11 scroll band on taller posts along Prairie Avenue only
the great stack: the photograph's clustered flues in carved stone; the record's plain brick stack in the same place
colour: the print is monochrome; the brick's red and the stone's fawn are the kit's

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
